subject: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing validation, canary cadence, and cutover checkpoints (Nebula Insights)
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@nebula-insights.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@nebula-insights.com
Date: 2027-08-02T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing validation, canary cadence, and cutover checkpoints (Nebula Insights)

Thanks for the call this morning, Soojin. Quick follow-up: our infra lead asked for a compact deliverable that maps committed QPS and 95th P50 token latency to GPU counts and suggested cutover windows. Attached is yesterday's token-level profile (30d window). Two asks: 1) can Redwood provide a conservative GPU count for steady-state + 2x burst, and 2) propose a 3-week canary cadence we can run with our SREs. Prefer PST times for cutovers.

Asha Reddy
Head of Platform
Nebula Insights

Attachments: nebula-metrics-snapshot-20270731.csv

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@nebula-insights.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing validation, canary cadence, and cutover checkpoints (Nebula Insights)

Asha — thanks for the metric dump. Marcus and I dug in and sketched a conservative plan. High level: for your 30d P50 token profile (peak sustained 180 qps, 95th single-thread latency ~120ms with our hosted gpt-medium family), we recommend starting with a dedicated pool sized for 220 sustained qps (headroom for short growth), with burst capacity to handle 2x peaks up to 440 qps using autoscale + transient pre-warm. Translating that into hardware: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent for steady-state inference with batching tuned to 16-32 tokens per request, and 4 additional A100 for buffer/burst (total 12), or 14 x A10s if you prefer cheaper cards but at higher unit count.

Proposed canary cadence (3 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): mirror subset of traffic (5%) to dedicated, dry-run DAG.
- Week 1 (canary-1): route 10% traffic to dedicated during low-traffic PST window (00:00-04:00). Monitor latency, KV hit-rate, error-rate.
- Week 2 (canary-2): increase to 30% during two rolling windows. Run throughput soak test (2h).
- Week 3 (cutover weekend): >90% route for full cutover in 2-step swap (gradual scaling).

I'll attach a short canary-playbook and the MAP. Question for you: are there any regulatory blackout dates in August?

— Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: canary-playbook.md, MAP-nebula-NEB-2027-08-v2.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-03T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing validation, canary cadence, and cutover checkpoints (Nebula Insights)

Looping infra/capacity. Couple of engineering notes we should surface to Asha:
- Kernel/quantization impact: if Nebula opts for int8 quantization we can reduce GPU count by ~25% subject to evals; call this an optional follow-up.
- KV cache considerations: their 30d profile shows a high prefix locality for conversational flows — we recommend enabling prefix caching in dedicated runtime to reduce effective throughput needs by ~12-18%.
- Service-level pods: dedicate 1x standby node per 6 active nodes for fast failover — factor into steady-state pool sizing.

I'll pull a quick sizing calc and share by EOD. Karthik

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@nebula-insights.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-03T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing validation, canary cadence, and cutover checkpoints (Nebula Insights)

Asha — attached is a quick sizing table (summary): steady-state 8 A100 equiv (220 qps sustain), burst pool 4 A100 equiv (2-minute autoscale targets), standby 2 nodes for HA, buffer for quantization/kv = +1. If Nebula prefers A10 fleet we estimate 11 steady + 5 burst + 2 standby.

Operational notes:
- Canary windows: prefer Sundays 01:00-05:00 PST and Wednesdays 02:00-04:00 PST to catch both low and mid-week behavior.
- Observability: We'll set per-route token-level tracing and a short retention (7d) for the canary.
- Fallback: maintain hosted API route as immediate fallback with traffic switch TTL of 30s and auto-fallback on error-rate >1.5% sustained for 3m.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Capacity & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nebula-sizing-summary-20270803.csv

From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@nebula-insights.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@nebula-insights.com, billing@nebula-insights.com
Date: 2027-08-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing validation, canary cadence, and cutover checkpoints (Nebula Insights)

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple clarifying items before we lock dates: 1) can you confirm the expected monthly $/token delta for A100-equivalent fleet vs hosted baseline with the proposed batching/kv settings? 2) For the standby nodes, do we need reserved capacity (paused) billing or will they be billed only when active? Finally, we'll need a signed MAP to kick-off procurement. I can share preferred weekend windows: Aug 28–29 or Sep 11–12.

Best,
Asha

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@nebula-insights.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-06T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing validation, canary cadence, and cutover checkpoints (Nebula Insights)

Asha — answers inline: 1) Pricing delta: with the proposed batching and KV caching we estimate a 42–48% reduction in per-token cost compared to your current hosted run rate at peak; we'll share a detailed pro forma in the MAP attachment (linked). 2) Standby nodes are part of the reserved pool and billed as part of the Dedicated commitment (they are reserved capacity, not on-demand); we can structure 1-month lookback options into the contract if you need a lower committed baseline.

Next steps:
- We'll push a revised MAP with the pro forma and the two candidate cutover weekends (Aug 28–29, Sep 11–12) by EOD tomorrow.
- Pre-cutover checklist: pre-warm cache (24h), confirm dkim/spf for traffic swap, and schedule a final canary rehearsal 72h before cutover.

Thanks — Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-nebula-NEB-2027-08-v3.pdf
